answer: Sybil resistance arises when trust propagates via bounded random walks over an attestation graph: honest attestations mix across well-connected regions, while an adversarial Sybil cluster is isolated by a sparse external cut of low conductance. Like a sonnet constrained by meter, conductance and min-cut transitivity bounds limit walk mass—and therefore aggregate voting weight—entering the cluster, preventing repeated attestations from amplifying a false signal to the network’s zenith.
